how: The opening proposal invites members to start a shared flag beneath an existing canvas landmark.
One member judges the proposed spot difficult because its occupant survived attacks, while another challenges that judgment using an earlier success.
Members propose a Georgian flag, identify existing small flags with uncertain survival, and revise the proposed location without recording an agreed decision.
Members choose between locations beneath and above the Ukrainian flag rather than settle a new picture design.
Testing a proposed spot against an occupant's endurance and an earlier successful change precedes a different suggested location without any reported loss of the proposed work.
A participant invokes having changed the occupying flag once to justify another attempt, supporting a reported earlier conversion rather than a verified fresh attack.
The proposer is visible, but the replies do not establish that others joined the placing.
Finding existing flags does not identify their builders or establish a build responding to this proposal.
Relative landmarks are coded, but the opening turn has an uncoded stretch, so this return cannot settle its full coordinate or template provision.
The attack-survival report concerns the occupying flag, while the continued existence of Georgian flags remains uncertain.
Claiming an earlier flag change does not identify placers or investigate who changed the room's own work.
The objection cites the occupied spot's resistance rather than a norm of sparing others or a request to stop attacking.
The location proposals do not record a border, truce, or deal negotiated with another room.
A revised proposed location does not establish that the room lost its work and then moved.
The prior-change claim justifies trying again rather than announces completion or celebrates the proposed flag.
The uncertain sighting leaves the proposed flag's eventual fate unresolved rather than supplying an event record.
The final location suggestion supplies no decision about keeping work or relationships beyond the canvas.
The warning and rebuttal mention endurance and prior success without mentioning scripts, spare accounts, or machine placement.
Every written reply in this exchange objects, gives a reasoned rebuttal, or qualifies and redirects the proposal rather than gives a bare joining answer.
The flag proposals and sighting do not record giving, requesting, or exchanging help with another room.
A Georgian flag found among hearts does not establish a coalition or an agreement between makers.
The rebuttal addresses a local warning about the proposed spot rather than trades taunts with a rival room.
Locating a proposed flag beside another does not establish a host ruling on a guest's work.
The call and discussion of locations do not show rules or boundaries being drawn around canvas talk.
The replies dispute feasibility and location without disputing who can bind placers to an agreement.
The cited turns concern proposed flag work rather than disputes over cleanup or the account preserved after placement ended.
The flag proposal and location suggestions do not supply April Fools parody framing.
Naming an occupying Soviet Union flag does not itself show an imported quarrel motivating action.
The proposal identifies a national flag without showing arguments about history, politics, or belonging beyond that flag.
The short exchange contains neither an explicit decision about organizing nor an explicit account of dispensing with such decisions.
The flags' names do not state a historical tie or ideology as the reason for changing the occupying flag.
The local location proposals do not identify anyone carrying a proposal between rooms.
The found flags are not linked to the opening call, so the call producing a build cannot be established.
The opening proposal already contains the call, leaving no separate starter-then-recruitment sequence.
The uncertain flag sighting supplies no sequence from this room building its mark to maintaining it.
A warning about another flag's endurance does not establish upkeep of the room's work leading to border talk.
The alternative location suggestion records neither a settled border nor restraint following one.
The report that an occupying flag survived attacks does not establish this room's upkeep producing machine placement.
An uncertain sighting does not establish a completed build followed by collective celebration.
The earlier-change claim serves a rebuttal and does not establish celebration producing preservation of the work.
The final suggestion leaves both the proposed work's fate and any later reuse undecided.
The objection concerns resistance at one spot, and the later suggestion does not establish a shortage causing an actual move.
The cited proposals supply no transition from design deliberation to an agreed pixel template.
The call receives reasoned objections and redirection rather than bare written acceptance within this exchange, while silent placing remains outside the test.
Uncertain flag survival does not establish upkeep straining the room and causing it to request outside help.
The proposed locations do not establish a negotiated border opening a channel for traded help.
The later reply recalls a change preceding the present call and does not establish a new attack caused by that call.
The objection concerns difficulty rather than restraint, leaving attack followed by restraint unobserved.
The warning and rebuttal invoke endurance and prior success rather than a truce or negotiation after an attack.
The claimed earlier conversion is discussed locally without a recorded contest in talk with its makers.
The sighting among hearts does not establish upkeep leading to a coalition.
The proposal and its location discussion do not establish a flood of calls producing host rules around canvas talk.
The feasibility dispute supplies neither a recorded agreement with another room nor a dispute over who can bind members to it.
